slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Level 3 is the richest tier of the Loire Valley course — from the dry Chenin Blanc of Anjou's schist slopes, to the finest botrytised sweet wines of the Layon Valley, and the twin flint-mineral powerhouses of Sancerre, you have journeyed through 32 white wine and sparkling AOCs. This assessment will test your mastery of the full Chenin Blanc craft spectrum, soil identification in the Central Loire, and the principles of Loire food pairing.

📝 Assessment Scope

All 11 lessons of Level 3 (lo-l3-1 to lo-l3-11), covering 32 white wine/sparkling AOCs

🎯 Number of Questions

5 comprehensive questions covering the Chenin Blanc sweetness system, botrytis science, Sancerre geology and pairing principles

🏆 Passing Standard

Answer 4 or more correctly (80%) to unlock Level 4
slides.1.title: Level 3 Comprehensive Assessment
slides.1.questions.0.question: In Vouvray's sweetness classification, what is the typical residual sugar range for 'Moelleux'?
slides.1.questions.0.explanation: Vouvray's sweetness levels: Sec (0–4 g/L), Demi-Sec (4–18 g/L), Moelleux (30–80 g/L, sometimes higher), Liquoreux (80 g/L+, botrytis or very sweet). 'Moelleux' (meaning 'soft') describes a wine with perceptible sweetness yet still balanced by Chenin Blanc's high acidity.
slides.1.questions.1.question: What is the defining winemaking feature of Muscadet Sèvre et Maine sur Lie?
slides.1.questions.1.options.0: Aged in new oak barrels for at least 18 months
slides.1.questions.1.options.1: Aged on dead yeast lees for at least 6 months before bottling, adding a brioche quality and creamy texture
slides.1.questions.1.options.3: Must complete fermentation in tuffeau underground caves
slides.1.questions.1.explanation: 'Sur Lie' is Muscadet's most important quality hallmark — the wine rests on dead yeast lees (at least 6 months; top cuvées up to 20+ months). Yeast autolysis imparts brioche, cream and a gentle prickle of retained CO₂, dramatically improving texture and complexity.
slides.1.questions.2.question: What is the deepest reason why Sancerre × Crottin de Chavignol is called 'the textbook terroir pairing'?
slides.1.questions.2.options.0: Both start with 'S', making them easy to remember
slides.1.questions.2.options.1: Both originate from the same Chavignol village — goats graze on meadows beside the vineyards, absorbing identical minerals, creating a deep 'terroir resonance'
slides.1.questions.2.options.2: The high fat content of the cheese allows drinkers to consume more Sancerre without getting drunk as quickly
slides.1.questions.2.options.3: French law requires Sancerre to be sold together with Crottin
slides.1.questions.2.explanation: The deepest reason is 'terroir resonance' — the goats of Chavignol village graze on the same meadows beside the Sancerre vineyards. Their milk (made into Crottin) and the neighbouring grapes (made into Sancerre) absorb the same minerals and botanical character. This shared origin creates the most natural possible harmony.
slides.1.questions.3.question: Which description most accurately captures the character of Savennières AOC?
slides.1.questions.3.options.0: Made from Sauvignon Blanc, similar in style to Sancerre
slides.1.questions.3.options.1: Made from 100% Chenin Blanc as a dry white, on Anjou's schist slopes; Nicolas Joly's biodynamic farming has established it as one of the world's greatest white wines
slides.1.questions.3.options.2: Primarily produces Cabernet Franc red wines — Anjou's most expensive red AOC
slides.1.questions.3.options.3: Made from Melon de Bourgogne, identical in style to Muscadet
slides.1.questions.3.explanation: Savennières AOC produces fully dry white wine from 100% Chenin Blanc, grown on a mix of schist and volcanic soils on Anjou's western slopes. Nicolas Joly's Clos de la Coulée de Serrant (farmed biodynamically) is the most celebrated producer, widely regarded as one of the world's greatest dry white wines.
slides.1.questions.4.question: What is the most critical distinction between Pouilly-Fumé and Pouilly-sur-Loire?
slides.1.questions.4.options.0: They are completely identical AOCs that simply share different names
slides.1.questions.4.options.1: Pouilly-Fumé uses Sauvignon Blanc (high quality); Pouilly-sur-Loire uses Chasselas (simpler quality) — both occupy the same geographic area
slides.1.questions.4.options.2: Pouilly-Fumé is from southern France; Pouilly-sur-Loire is from northern France
slides.1.questions.4.options.3: Pouilly-sur-Loire is sweet-style; Pouilly-Fumé is dry-style
slides.1.questions.4.explanation: Pouilly-Fumé AOC (Sauvignon Blanc) and Pouilly-sur-Loire AOC (Chasselas) cover exactly the same geographic area (the town of Pouilly-sur-Loire in Nièvre département) but use different grape varieties. Pouilly-Fumé with Sauvignon Blanc is the prestige AOC; Pouilly-sur-Loire with Chasselas is simpler, now almost abandoned, with a shrinking planted area.
